title: Beyond prompting
message: Visual tools for self-directed learning with artificial intelligence
notes: Titolo comune per i tre eventi a Vilnius, novembre2026. Il Forum si svolge11–12novembre; incontroMRU10novembre e docenti13novembre. Selezionare il percorso dalla copertina: cambia ordine, scelta delle slide e timebox, mantenendo un unico set di contenuti. Il pacchetto didattico è una proposta informata dalle fonti, non un metodo clinico o un protocollo unitario già validato.

message: Tenure-Track Assistant Professor

Semantic AI & knowledge graphs
Digital mental health
Applied data systems

cards.title: Predictive analytics

cards.title: Responsible AI
cards.body: Design focused on people, evidence and system limits

cards.title: Modular solutions
cards.body: Components integrated into existing workflows

Presentare in circa 30 secondi il collegamento tra ricerca universitaria e strumenti di IA e analisi dei dati per le organizzazioni. I tre ambiti sintetizzano i servizi descritti dal sito ufficiale e dalla scheda istituzionale UniMiB: analisi predittiva, IA etica e soluzioni modulari. Fonti consultate il 31 ottobre 2026.

title: Today’s route
message: Connect learning decisions, evidence, visual tools and responsible practice.
body: Learning decisions and evidence
Visual guidance
Risks and inclusive access
Designing a learning activity
notes: Indice dopo la presentazione del relatore e di Whattadata. Dichiarare che si lavorerà con carta o testo e non occorre creare account. Esplicitare i due risultati attesi: progettare un aiuto utile e scegliere una verifica dell’apprendimento. Il percorso breve salta gli approfondimenti mantenendo questo stesso ordine.

title: What would count as learning?
message: Illustrative classroom scenario: solving a maths problem with AI.
body: What would you ask the student to explain or try next?
Choose one check. Think, write, or discuss with a partner.
notes: Scenario didattico illustrativo originale: uno studente usa l’IA per risolvere un problema di matematica e consegna prima una risposta corretta. Non abbiamo ancora osservato se sa spiegare i passaggi. La consegna chiede al pubblico di proporre una verifica della comprensione, per esempio motivare un passaggio o affrontare un problema simile senza la risposta generata. Non è un risultato empirico né un test diagnostico. Accogliere una risposta nei percorsi brevi, due nel Forum; non raccogliere nomi o punteggi. Conservare gli ausili di accesso. Una verifica immediata non dimostra ritenzione duratura; il Forum può distinguere anche un controllo differito.
quote: A student uses AI to solve a maths problem. The answer is correct and arrives faster. We have not heard the student explain the steps.

title: Session outcomes
message: Design one learning activity with a clear goal, a visible process and an independent content check.
body: Choose the skill the learner should develop
Make the learning decisions visible
Specify evidence, access options and limits
notes: Slide di esplicitazione degli obiettivi nel Forum. Nei percorsi brevi incorporare questi obiettivi oralmente nell’indice S03. Gli obiettivi sono scelte progettuali del seminario, non esiti già dimostrati della combinazione AI e canvas.
explanation: By the end, you will have a small activity you can try in your own setting. Its design will show what the learner decides and how you will check understanding.

cards.title: Set a learning goal
cards.body: Name what the learner should explain or do. Using an AI tool is an action, not the learning goal.

cards.title: Make the process visible
cards.body: Record a first attempt, the help used and the decisions made. Keep a trace that the learner can review.

cards.title: Plan the check and access
cards.body: Choose an observable explanation or task. State the limits of the evidence and keep the access support people need.

title: Self-direction and self-regulation
message: Learners can regulate an assigned task while also learning to choose goals and resources.
body: Self-directed learning: identify needs, goals and resources
Self-regulated learning: plan, monitor and evaluate learning
Autonomy can include teachers, peers and access support
notes: Distinzione concettuale da Loyens e Panadero, non tassonomia rigida. Usare un esempio: uno studente regola una lettura assegnata; in un progetto autodiretto sceglie anche la domanda e le fonti. Con docenti tenere l’esempio concreto e breve. Evitare di equiparare autonomia a lavoro solitario.

cards.title: Self-direction
cards.body: Identify your needs and choose goals and resources. Example: choose a question for a project, then decide which sources to investigate.

cards.title: Self-regulation
cards.body: Plan, monitor and evaluate your learning. Example: plan an assigned reading, check what you understand and change your approach when needed.

takeaway: Autonomy can include teachers, peers and access support
explanation: A learner can plan and check a task set by a teacher. Self-direction also includes choosing the learning question, goals and resources.

title: The learning regulation cycle
message: Planning, monitoring and reflection guide decisions before, during and after a task.
body: Plan: What am I trying to understand?
Monitor: What is working, and what needs checking?
Reflect: What changed, and what will I try next?
notes: Disegnare un ciclo originale con tre fasi e frecce etichettate. È una semplificazione didattica dei modelli SRL, non una nuova teoria e non una misura psicometrica. Collegare ogni fase a una decisione dello studente e, con docenti, al modellamento del pensiero ad alta voce.

cards.title: Plan
cards.body: Set a goal and choose a first approach. What am I trying to understand?

cards.title: Monitor
cards.body: Inspect your progress and check uncertain claims. What is working, and what needs changing?

cards.title: Reflect
cards.body: Compare your result with the goal. What changed, and what will I try next?

takeaway: A recurring cycle, not a fixed sequence

title: Four different outcomes
message: Assisted performance, unaided performance, retention and transfer answer different questions.
body: Assisted task: How good is the product?
Independent content check: What can the learner explain or do?
Retention: What remains after an interval?
Transfer: What carries over to a new task?
notes: Fissare il vocabolario per tutti gli studi successivi. Una prova immediata senza AI non è già prova di durata; fiducia, soddisfazione e tracce di processo sono altri esiti. Conservare ausili di accesso nelle verifiche del contenuto. Non definire uno studente autonomo da un singolo punteggio.

cards.title: Assisted product
cards.body: Check the quality of the answer while help is available, such as an AI-assisted essay.

cards.title: Independent check
cards.body: Ask the learner to explain or do the target task without the content answer. Keep access support.

cards.title: Retention
cards.body: Check what the learner remembers after an interval, beyond the immediate end of the activity.

cards.title: Transfer
cards.body: Ask the learner to use the idea in a different task or case. Check the explanation as well.

title: Better practice can hide a weaker independent test
message: In one school mathematics RCT, unrestricted AI improved practice but reduced unaided exam performance.
body: About 1,000 pupils · one Turkish school · four sessions
GPT Base: practice +48%; unaided exam −17%
GPT Tutor: practice +127%; no significant unaided exam advantage
All percentages are relative to the control group
notes: Bastani: dichiarare subito contesto e confronto. Tutor con guardrail ha ridotto il danno osservato nella condizione Base, senza dimostrare un guadagno all’esame autonomo. Non trasformare le variazioni relative in punti percentuali; non generalizzare a tutte le materie o ai modelli attuali. Tecnologia raccolta nel 2023; nessuna ritenzione lunga.
guardrails: No significant advantage is not proof of universal equivalence.
context: Classroom RCT · about 1,000 pupils · one Turkish school · four sessions
result_note: Relative changes versus control, not percentage points
finding: GPT Tutor: +127% in practice; no significant unaided exam advantage.
limit: Immediate outcomes in one setting; long-term retention was not tested.

title: A designed tutor improved immediate test performance
message: A carefully designed tutor outperformed active classroom instruction in two university physics lessons.
body: 194 Harvard students · randomized crossover
Designed AI tutor versus an active classroom lesson
Higher immediate post-test performance
No delayed retention test
notes: Kestin: affiancare questo caso favorevole a Bastani, senza fare una graduatoria fra studi. Il pacchetto include progettazione didattica, ritmo individuale e feedback: non isola una proprietà generale del modello. 316 indica osservazioni post-test aggregate, non numero di persone. Non usare il titolo dello studio come promessa universale.
context: Randomized crossover · 194 Harvard students · two physics lessons
finding: A designed AI tutor outperformed an active classroom lesson on immediate post-tests.
limit: The comparison involved instructional packages. No delayed retention test; 316 observations are not 316 participants.

title: The comparison is part of the finding
message: Different tutors, tasks, controls and measures can produce different outcomes.
body: What did the AI actually do?
What did the comparison group receive?
Was the outcome assisted, independent or delayed?
notes: Nel Forum confrontare A01 e A02 con tre domande, non confrontare direttamente le dimensioni degli effetti. Nei percorsi brevi incorporare queste cautele nelle note S09–S10. La critica metodologica non annulla automaticamente risultati positivi; impedisce di attribuire all’AI ciò che può dipendere dalla didattica del pacchetto.
takeaway: A study supports a bounded claim about a particular comparison

cards.title: AI support
cards.body: What did the AI actually do: give answers, ask questions or guide practice? These are different forms of support.

cards.title: Comparison
cards.body: What did the other group receive: no help, a teacher, another tutor or a different lesson?

cards.title: Outcome
cards.body: Was the task completed with help, independently or after a delay? Keep the claim tied to the measure.

title: A better essay did not establish better transfer
message: In one writing experiment, ChatGPT improved the essay without a significant advantage in knowledge or transfer.
body: 117 university students · Chinese L1 / English L2
Four conditions: ChatGPT, human expert, analytics, no support
Better assisted essay; no significant knowledge or transfer advantage
notes: Fan è il principale ponte SSH per il percorso universitario. Un’attività di laboratorio e gruppi piccoli: non estendere a tutte le pratiche di scrittura, alla ricerca storica o all’argomentazione filosofica. Metacognitive laziness è l’interpretazione degli autori, non una diagnosi né una prova di danno al cervello.
context: Randomized writing study · 117 university students · Chinese L1 / English L2
finding: ChatGPT improved the assisted essay. Knowledge and transfer showed no significant advantage.
limit: One laboratory task and small groups. “Metacognitive laziness” is an interpretation, not a diagnosis.

title: More prompting did not improve every school outcome
message: SRL-oriented prompting did not show a clear knowledge or strategy advantage over standard ChatGPT in one school RCT.
body: 371 pupils · grades 7–9 · physics and English
Six 45-minute lessons; three AI conditions
No significant advantage in knowledge, strategies, interest or effort
notes: Fütterer: esito nullo utile per insegnanti; il confronto è fra tre configurazioni AI, non AI contro nessuna AI. Misura di conoscenza breve, tre item per materia. Non concludere che la progettazione dei prompt sia inutile in generale. Nel percorso universitario è approfondimento non proiettato.
context: Preregistered RCT · 371 pupils · grades 7–9 · six physics/English lessons
finding: Two prompting approaches showed no significant advantage over standard ChatGPT in the main outcomes.
limit: All groups used AI. This does not establish equivalence between AI and no AI; knowledge tests were brief.

title: Emotional support and knowledge are different outcomes
message: A supportive tone can affect the experience without demonstrating a knowledge advantage.
body: 144 upper-secondary psychology students · three AI conditions
Some emotional and SRL process benefits
No significant knowledge, transfer or follow-up advantage
notes: A07: studio recente, due scuole danesi, singola attività, follow-up incompleto. Nessun gruppo senza AI. Supporto emotivo simulato mediante prompt: non attribuire al chatbot comprensione delle emozioni, diagnosi o funzione clinica. La partecipazione a riflessioni personali deve rimanere volontaria.
context: Preregistered RCT · 144 upper-secondary psychology students · three AI conditions
finding: Some emotional and self-regulation benefits; no significant knowledge or transfer advantage.
limit: No group without AI. Four-week follow-up was incomplete; this was not clinical emotional understanding.

title: Proactive guidance helped learners interpret visual data
message: Proactive AI guidance improved interpretation of visual learning analytics in a specific task
body: Proactive AI questions and feedback outperformed passive help and narrative scaffolding in this task
Benefits remained on the immediate test after support removal
notes: Studio Yan et al. (2025), Computers & Education, DOI10.1016/j.compedu.2025.105322. RCT online controllato con117studenti, visualizzazioni di una simulazione infermieristica. Domande/feedback proattivi superano agente passivo e data storytelling; beneficio nel test immediato dopo rimozione. Il passivo non risulta significativamente superiore allo scaffolding non-IA. Non sono esiti clinici o ritenzione a settimane. PDF originale Monash, pp.1,11,19. Non valida il canvas di questo seminario.
guardrails: Randomized online laboratory study with117 higher-education learners
Immediate post-removal test, not delayed retention
Specific visualizations and comprehension questions; not general critical thinking
context: Randomized online laboratory study · 117 higher-education learners · about one hour
finding: Proactive AI outperformed passive help and narrative scaffolding; the benefit remained immediately after support removal.
limit: No delayed retention test; specific visualizations and comprehension tasks, not general critical thinking.

title: Choose a visual form for the task
message: Different representations expose different kinds of reasoning.
body: Concept map: concepts and labelled relationships
Argument map: claim, reasons, evidence and objections
Learning path: decisions, checks and next steps
notes: Mostrare tre piccoli esempi originali riferiti alla stessa domanda AI/studio. Spiegare oralmente ogni relazione; rendere disponibile il testo equivalente. Non confondere mappe concettuali con qualunque mind map ramificata e non invocare presunti studenti visivi. La scelta segue compito e preferenze di accesso.

cards.title: Concept map
cards.body: Connect concepts and label each relationship. Use it to explain how ideas relate, rather than just grouping keywords.

cards.title: Argument map
cards.body: Separate a claim from its reasons, evidence and objections. Use it to inspect what supports a conclusion.

cards.title: Learning path
cards.body: Show the goal, attempts, support and checks. Use it to decide what to do next and why.

takeaway: Choose the representation for the task; offer a structured text equivalent
explanation: Choose the form that makes the required reasoning visible. A structured text list can express the same relationships when a diagram creates a barrier.

title: Map construction and retrieval
message: A map can support learning, but its presence or polish does not establish learning.
body: Map studies vary by task and comparison
Retrieval practice can outperform mapping while viewing the text
Rebuilding relationships from memory is a different activity
notes: Affiancare la base meta-analitica sulle mappe a Karpicke/Blunt e Lenski. Non dire che recupero supera sempre qualunque mappa o che le mappe sono inutili. Qualità strutturale, completezza e bellezza estetica non sono lo stesso costrutto. Il confronto dei moderatori costruzione/studio non è una randomizzazione diretta fra i due formati.

cards.title: Construct a map
cards.body: Explain each link instead of copying keywords. Ask which relationship needs a source, a condition or a clearer meaning.

cards.title: Retrieve and rebuild
cards.body: Put the source aside and rebuild the ideas from memory. Then reopen it to check missing or mistaken relationships.

takeaway: A map is an activity, not a guarantee of learning. Avoid fixed “learning style” labels.

title: Which link needs evidence?
message: Add a condition, a source or a counterexample
body: Fast answers
Understanding
Independence
notes: Micro-attività estesa solo nel Forum: dare trenta secondi di lettura e raccogliere due correzioni. La catena è un esempio deliberatamente incompleto scritto per il seminario, non una citazione. Inserire relazioni come may support e requires. La stessa idea torna nella revisione dell’attività principale, senza richiedere questa slide nei flussi brevi.
output: One repaired relationship, with its reason
explanation: Read each arrow as a claim. Choose one link and add a reason, a condition or a counterexample that changes how strongly you would trust it.

title: The Learning Path Canvas
message: Decisions that can be inspected and revised
body: Goal and starting point
First attempt
Allowed support
Sources and uncertainty
Independent content check
Reflection
notes: Presentare solo tre gruppi di campi; il foglio completo è nella consegna S34. Canvas originale informato dai framework, non scala psicometrica o protocollo validato come pacchetto. Nei flussi brevi saltare l’anteprima: la spiegazione avviene durante il lavoro. Offrire elenco lineare anziché obbligare a disegnare.
takeaway: Original workshop template; not a validated psychological scale
explanation: Use these six fields to record a learning plan. Show which decisions belong to the learner, what help is allowed and how understanding will be checked.

cards.title: Goal and starting point
cards.body: What should I learn? What do I know?

cards.title: First attempt
cards.body: Record an approach before asking for content help.

cards.title: Allowed support
cards.body: Choose questions, hints or feedback; state the boundary.

cards.title: Sources and uncertainty
cards.body: Check the source; name what remains uncertain.

cards.title: Independent content check
cards.body: Explain or apply the idea without the answer.

cards.title: Reflection
cards.body: What changed? What will I try next?

title: Guidance, fading and access support
message: Reduce content help when appropriate while preserving access to the task.
body: Model a strategy and observe the learner’s response
Adjust and gradually reduce content support
Keep the access accommodations the learner needs
notes: Distinguere ostacolo di accesso e capacità oggetto dell’apprendimento. Un lettore di schermo o una traduzione non è automaticamente delega del ragionamento. Darvishi riguarda AI non generativa: non presentarlo come esperimento su ChatGPT. Non ogni offloading è dannoso; riduzione progressiva e checklist non garantiscono da sole autonomia.

cards.title: Model the strategy
cards.body: Show how you make a decision and check a source. Let the learner see the reasoning behind the answer.

cards.title: Adjust the help
cards.body: Observe the next attempt. Offer a question or hint, then reduce content help when the learner is ready.

cards.title: Preserve access
cards.body: Keep screen readers, dictation, translation and other agreed support. Separate the thinking being checked from barriers to participation.

takeaway: Reducing content help does not mean removing access support
explanation: Show the reasoning, observe an attempt and adjust the help. Reduce support that supplies the content answer while keeping the accommodations needed to access the task.

title: Fluent answers and fabricated references
message: Verify the source and its relevance, not just the form of the citation.
body: Open the original source
Check title, author, date and DOI
Find the passage that supports the claim
notes: A17 documenta citazioni inventate in modelli del 2023; non proiettare i tassi come affidabilità dei prodotti attuali. Mostrare un registro claim–source–locator–verdict su un estratto verificato, non un riferimento falso attribuito a uno studioso reale. Anche un link esistente può non sostenere la frase.

cards.title: Open the original
cards.body: Check the title, authors, date and DOI. A well-formatted citation does not show that the source exists.

cards.title: Read the passage
cards.body: Find the result that supports the claim. Check who was studied, what was compared and when it was measured.

cards.title: Check its status
cards.body: Look for corrections or retractions on the publisher’s page. Recheck the claim if the source has changed.

takeaway: A fluent explanation or generated citation is not verification
explanation: A reference can look correct and still be false or irrelevant. Open the original, read the supporting passage and check whether the publication has been corrected.

title: Reflection before accepting AI advice
message: A short reflection intervention reduced acceptance of wrong advice in one immediate decision experiment.
body: 342 university students · one Chinese university
Wrong-advice acceptance: 62.4% with free chat; 39.7% with reflection
Immediate task outcome; no evidence of lasting transfer
notes: Ren: confrontare percentuali di accettazione, non interpretarle come riduzione generale del rischio. Il campione include SSH ma non dimostra un effetto specifico di quel sottogruppo. Richiedere ragionamento iniziale e motivo della revisione richiede tempo. A05 è survey di lavoratori: sostiene associazioni, non perdita causale di capacità. Nei docenti incorporare la risposta pratica nell’attività invece di proiettare questa slide.
context: Randomized experiment · 342 students · one Chinese university
finding: Reflection prompts reduced acceptance of wrong advice in this immediate task.
limit: A specific short decision task. Lasting transfer was not established.

title: Language, bias and missing perspectives
message: A polished rewrite can remove a voice or narrow the available perspectives.
body: Whose language or perspective is missing?
Compare meaning, uncertainty and cultural voice
Do not infer a person’s ability from a generated judgement
notes: Usare il caso sperimentale dei bias dialettali come esempio circoscritto, evitando generalizzazioni a tutte le lingue. Per SSH collegare alla scelta delle fonti e alla pluralità interpretativa; per docenti evitare riscritture che trasformano registro in deficit. Non mostrare insulti o diagnosi sintetiche non necessari.

cards.title: Language
cards.body: Check whether a rewrite keeps the writer’s meaning and cultural voice. More standard wording is not always a better fit.

cards.title: Perspective
cards.body: Ask which sources, experiences or interpretations are missing. Compare the account with other relevant evidence.

cards.title: Judgement
cards.body: Do not use generated text to infer a person’s ability. People need reasons they can inspect and challenge.

takeaway: Compare sources and interpretations; prompting cannot guarantee fairness
explanation: When using a rewrite or generated judgement, compare meaning, uncertainty and voice. Ask whose perspective is absent before accepting the result.

title: Privacy and institutional responsibility
message: Choose the data and the setting before opening a tool.
body: Use public or synthetic material for the activity
Check institutional rules, account settings and age requirements
Keep responsibility for consequential decisions with people
notes: Non caricare elaborati identificabili, diagnosi, fotografie o conversazioni personali. Distinguere documenti istituzionali, regole locali e dichiarazioni del fornitore; nessuna promessa generale di riservatezza. Evitare inferenze automatiche su emozioni e bisogni. Il dossier non sostituisce procedure o verifiche dell’istituzione.

cards.title: Public or synthetic
cards.body: Choose examples that do not identify learners. Do not upload diagnoses, identifiable student work or private conversations in a demo.

cards.title: Institutional checks
cards.body: Review the approved setting, account requirements and handling of data. Resolve these choices before asking learners to use a tool.

cards.title: Human responsibility
cards.body: Keep decisions that affect people with responsible staff. Do not ask AI to infer a learner’s diagnosis or emotions.

takeaway: Avoid uploading diagnoses, identifiable work or private conversations in a demo
explanation: Use public or made-up material in this workshop. Before real classroom use, follow your institution’s process for accounts, age requirements and data handling.

title: Access support belongs in the learning design
message: Preserve the learning goal while offering more than one route to participate.
body: Map or structured list
Written or spoken response
Independent content check with access accommodations
notes: Principio operativo UDL, non evidenza che ogni opzione aiuti ogni diagnosi. Non chiedere pubblicamente una diagnosi o la motivazione di un bisogno. Esplicitare che ritmo, lingua, interazione e formato possono cambiare senza eliminare la richiesta di ragionare. Conservare ausili anche nelle verifiche indipendenti.

cards.title: More than one format
cards.body: Offer the diagram and a structured text version. Keep the concepts, relationships and reading order available in both.

cards.title: More than one response
cards.body: Allow a written, spoken or visual explanation. Judge the reasoning needed for the goal, rather than the format alone.

cards.title: The same learning goal
cards.body: Keep access accommodations during the content check. Ask what the learner understands while removing avoidable barriers.

takeaway: Choice of access is not a fixed learning style or a lower intellectual goal
explanation: Keep the intellectual goal clear while offering different ways to take part. Change the format or access route without removing the reasoning the task is meant to develop.

title: Can someone recover the argument without the diagram?
message: Describe the reasoning, not only the appearance
body: Label the relationships
Describe the structure in text
Check reading order, contrast and captions
notes: Mostrare due versioni originali dello stesso argomento: nodi/colori senza parole-legame e testo ordinato con relazioni esplicite. Audit del materiale, non simulazione di disabilità. Descrivere oralmente ogni elemento. Eventuali rapporti di contrasto WCAG vanno applicati al formato concreto, senza dichiarare conformità non valutata.
output: One barrier and one change that preserves the argument

title: An image description can invent a consequential detail
message: Who can verify the description?
body: In an ASSETS interview study, blind participants described benefits and errors in generative AI
An example added an unsupported guide-dog role and confused objects held
notes: Caso circoscritto di R16, non tasso di errore corrente e non argomento per escludere l’uso assistivo. Raccontare senza riprodurre la fotografia. Lo studio riporta benefici percepiti e difficoltà di controllo; non presupporre che l’utente possa verificare guardando l’originale. Prevedere accesso a una fonte o descrizione umana controllata.
takeaway: Faster alt text does not by itself establish accuracy or equivalent access
explanation: In an interview study, blind participants described useful AI help and errors. Consider how someone can verify a detail when the description is their route to the image.

title: Participation choices
message: No account, diagram drawing or personal disclosure is required.
body: Work alone or with a partner
Use a map, a structured list or a spoken explanation
Ask for clarification, more time or a different format
notes: Nel Forum usare anche come minuto di pausa cognitiva e ricapitolazione, compreso nel tempo. Nessuna richiesta di login. Nei flussi brevi dare queste scelte nella consegna S31. Fornire prima dell’evento testi editabili e glossario; non affidare tutte le informazioni a un QR code.

cards.title: Work alone or together
cards.body: Write your own proposal or discuss it with a partner. You can also use a partner as a coach.

cards.title: Choose a format
cards.body: Use labelled arrows, a structured list or a spoken explanation. Make the decisions and their reasons clear.

cards.title: Ask for a change
cards.body: Ask for clarification, more time or another format. You do not need to share a diagnosis publicly.

takeaway: No public diagnosis or account creation is required
explanation: Choose a way to participate that works for you. No account, diagram drawing or personal disclosure is required; the activity focuses on reasoning rather than speed.

title: Tool roles and selection
message: Select tools for a learning function, then verify access and data conditions.
body: Paper or text editor: record and revise the learning path
Conversational assistant: question, hint or critique
Source notebook: compare claims with supplied passages
notes: Esempi documentati nel catalogo: ChatGPT per dialogo, NotebookLM/Gemini Notebook per fonti, CmapTools o Excalidraw per rappresentazioni. Non attribuire miglioramento didattico alle sole funzioni. Condizioni e nomi vanno ricontrollati prima dell’evento; nessun account o test live è stato eseguito nella ricerca. Il percorso base usa solo carta e schede.

cards.title: CmapTools / Excalidraw
cards.body: Draft concepts and label each link. Keep a structured text version so the diagram is not the only way to follow the reasoning.

cards.title: Conversational assistant
cards.body: After a first attempt, ask for one question, hint or critique. Keep responsibility for the answer and for checking it.

cards.title: Source notebook
cards.body: Supply the study passage and compare it with your claim. Open the original source to check whether it supports the conclusion.

takeaway: Choose by task, access and data conditions; every activity also works on paper
explanation: Start with the learning action you need, then choose a tool. These are examples of functions; they do not establish that a product improves learning.

title: A prepared example: check the outcome
message: Prepared illustration, not an observed live AI response
body: Prepare a public source and a clearly labelled illustrative response
Show how to check one claim against the passage
Keep a text version and an offline route
notes: Esempio preparato e dichiarato, non output osservato in diretta. La scheda fornita parafrasa Kestin et al.2025, DOI10.1038/s41598-025-97652-6:194partecipanti, post-test immediati, nessun test ritardato. Chiedere quale parola nella promessa long-term retention non è sostenuta. Aprire il passaggio originale o la scheda verificata locale; il notebook e il prompt non sostituiscono la verifica. La demo live è facoltativa e usa solo contenuti pubblici o sintetici.
prompt: My claim is: “An AI tutor improves long-term retention.” Ask one question that helps me check it against the supplied study.
response: Which delayed test did the study include? Its reported post-test was immediate.
takeaway: Check the original source. A good prompt still needs verification.
supplied: Kestin et al.2025 · study cardS42: immediate post-tests with194 students; no delayed retention test

title: Design a responsible study activity
message: Your institution is considering AI for independent study
body: Choose a familiar topic
Design one small learning activity
Specify what you would observe before expanding it
notes: Consegna comune ai tre pubblici. Studenti/ricercatori possono scegliere una spiegazione o un’argomentazione; docenti una capacità nel proprio curricolo. Nessuna necessità di usare AI realmente. Distribuire canvas lineare e schede A01/A02; aggiungere A03 come opzione SSH. Dare un esempio non controverso se un gruppo non sceglie un tema.
output: A learning goal, a support boundary and an observable check
explanation: Use this claim: “A better AI-assisted answer proves better understanding.” Design a short activity to test it, or choose a topic from your own teaching.

title: Your first attempt
message: Record your own goal and initial approach before receiving content help.
body: By the end, the learner will be able to …
My first approach is …
I would look for evidence of …
notes: Lavoro iniziale individuale senza assistenza generativa sul contenuto, conservando gli ausili di accesso. Non è una valutazione e non si raccolgono risposte. Forum3min, università/docenti2min. Facilitare chi preferisce spiegare oralmente a un partner. L’esempio deve descrivere una capacità osservabile, non semplicemente usare un’app.
output: A first proposal before asking for content help

title: Check what the evidence supports
message: Choose a finding that is relevant to your activity
body: Who took part? What was the comparison?
What outcome was actually measured?
This suggests …; it does not establish …
notes: Le schede stampabili sono S41–S43. Non chiedere ricerche web sul momento; tutte le informazioni necessarie sono fornite. Forum confronta almeno due carte; università può scegliere A03 e una carta contrastante; docenti A01/A02 con richiamo orale A06. Il relatore fa un esempio di percentuale relativa e di prova immediata.
output: One bounded claim and one limitation
explanation: Open one study card. Complete: “This finding suggests …, but it does not establish …”. Connect the claim to your proposed activity.

title: Build the learning path
message: Which decisions stay with the learner?
body: Goal
First attempt
Useful support
Source check
Independent check
Reflection
notes: Forum6min, università4min, docenti5min. Il canvas completo è nei campi handout qui sotto, non da proiettare tutto in caratteri piccoli. Se emerge una barriera di accesso cambiare formato o canale, mantenendo l’obiettivo. Non valutare la bellezza del diagramma e non far dipendere l’esito dalla velocità.
output: A learning path, using labelled arrows or a structured list
explanation: Write one decision per field. Use labelled arrows or a numbered list.

cards.title: Goal
cards.body: State what the learner should explain or do.

cards.title: First attempt
cards.body: Record the learner’s approach before content help.

cards.title: Useful support
cards.body: Choose a question, hint or feedback boundary.

cards.title: Source check
cards.body: Identify the passage that supports the claim.

cards.title: Independent check
cards.body: Explain or apply the idea; keep access support.

cards.title: Reflection
cards.body: Name what changed and one next step.

title: Revise a weak study recommendation
message: Prepared illustration · deliberately incomplete
body: What is missing?
Add a source check, an explanation or a new application
notes: Raccomandazione sintetica deliberatamente debole, scritta per l’attività: etichettarla così sulla slide, senza attribuirla a ChatGPT o a uno studioso. Riconoscere che una sintesi può essere un punto di partenza, poi chiedere come verificare contenuto e apprendimento. Forum3min, università1min, docenti2min; raccogliere una revisione concreta.
output: One revision that adds an observable learner action
quote: Use AI to produce a summary, read it twice, and judge understanding by how clear it feels.
explanation: Read the recommendation below as a deliberately incomplete example. Replace one passive step with an action that lets you observe what the learner understands.

title: Explain the decision without the model answer
message: Check the target content while keeping access accommodations.
body: Close or turn over the content answer
Explain one decision and its reason
Name a limit or apply the idea to a new case
notes: Non togliere lettori di schermo, dettatura, traduzione o altri ausili necessari. Se un modello AI fornisce l’argomentazione al posto del partecipante, sostituirlo temporaneamente con un canale di accesso che conservi il ragionamento della persona. Partner può ascoltare o annotare; non attribuire da questa prova una competenza stabile o un voto.
output: A reasoned explanation, in a written or spoken format
takeaway: Keep screen readers, dictation, translation and approved accommodations

title: Debrief the learning path
message: Evaluate the decisions and evidence, not the appearance of the output.
body: What did the support help you do?
What did you still have to decide?
What would show retention or transfer?
Who might be excluded?
notes: Forum4min: ascoltare due gruppi, discutere un miglioramento e un’esclusione. Università2,5min: una proposta SSH e una controspiegazione. Docenti2min: una scelta didattica e un adattamento accessibile. Nessuna risposta obbligatoriamente pro-AI o contro-AI. Se si parla di fiducia, collegarla a una spiegazione osservabile senza usarla come unico esito.
output: One change to your activity after the discussion

title: One decision, one later check
message: Try one bounded activity and decide what evidence would justify repeating or changing it.
body: Name a familiar learning goal
Choose a later recall or transfer task
Ask learners what helped and what created barriers
notes: Proposta progettuale, non protocollo sperimentale. Con docenti scegliere come osservare un errore tipico e programmare un controllo successivo nella routine; con universitari applicare a una lettura o argomentazione. Un piccolo pilot non prova causalità. La raccolta di dati deve seguire le procedure dell’istituzione, non essere improvvisata nel seminario.
output: A small follow-up you can try in your setting

title: Keep the learning decisions visible
message: Research, prompts and printable materials
body: Separate the product from the evidence of learning
Make decisions visible and revisable
Keep human judgement and access support
notes: Tornare alla domanda iniziale e condividere il dossier e i materiali stampabili. Dossier verificato: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1bga8afM8CtVytu2HqBHhL73TU8YoV4IkxsyA7AZa4cY/edit . Archivio: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/19gOrOPe4khWqyMRn0MKCQ1NwE0DQ9ZNW . Il pacchetto locale contiene testi equivalenti e prompt; le tre frasi sono sintesi editoriali, non citazioni letterali.
explanation: Use these three decisions when planning your next activity. The links below provide the research dossier, classroom packet, prompt bank and an accessible text version.

cards.title: Check the learning
cards.body: Assess what the learner can explain or do. Keep the assisted product separate from retention and transfer.

cards.title: Show the decisions
cards.body: Record goals, attempts, support and source checks. Use reflection to decide what to revise or try next.

cards.title: Keep people and access
cards.body: Keep human responsibility for consequential choices. Preserve access support and offer more than one way to participate.

title: Questions and discussion
message: Which learning decision will you make visible?
body: Which goal needs support?
Which claim needs evidence?
Which barrier needs another route?
notes: Tempi inclusi nei totali: Forum 6,5 min, università 4 min, docenti 2,5 min. Per domande empiriche tornare alle schede e non inventare risultati di sottogruppo. Le carte in appendice non sono tempo aggiuntivo: usarle dentro questo spazio. Se emerge una questione non verificata, dichiararla e annotarla per controllo successivo.

title: Evidence card: school mathematics
message: Assisted practice and independent exam performance can diverge.
body: Bastani et al. (2025), PNAS · classroom RCT
About 1,000 pupils, one Turkish school, four sessions
Base: practice +48%, unaided exam −17%; Tutor: practice +127%, no significant exam advantage
Relative changes vs control; immediate outcomes, not long-term retention
notes: Carta da stampare o distribuire in testo editabile per S33; non slide da aggiungere alla cronologia. Confronto con libri/appunti. Precisare la natura relativa delle percentuali; Tutor riduce il danno, non dimostra guadagno indipendente. Fonte e passaggi A01, Abstract/ExperimentalDesign/Table1/Discussion.

title: Evidence card: a designed physics tutor
message: A designed AI tutor improved the immediate test in a specific university comparison.
body: Kestin et al. (2025), Scientific Reports · randomized crossover
194 Harvard students, two introductory physics lessons
Designed tutor versus active classroom instruction: higher immediate post-test performance
Different instructional packages; no delayed retention test
notes: Carta per S33 e domande finali, non tempo aggiuntivo. Non confrontare direttamente dimensione dell’effetto con Bastani: materie, popolazioni, tempi e controlli differenti. 194 persone; 316 osservazioni aggregate. Fonte A02 Results/Discussion/Methods.

title: Evidence card: writing and transfer
message: An improved assisted essay did not establish a knowledge or transfer advantage.
body: Fan et al. (2025), BJET · randomized experiment
117 university students, Chinese L1 / English L2, four conditions
ChatGPT improved the essay; no significant knowledge or transfer advantage
One laboratory task and small groups; not a diagnosis of cognitive harm
notes: Carta opzionale SSH per S33; Forum può confrontarla alle altre, docenti possono usarla solo se scrittura è il tema scelto. Quattro condizioni ChatGPT/esperto/analytics/nessun supporto. Non presentare l’interpretazione metacognitive laziness come una diagnosi. Fonte A03 Methods/Results/PractitionerNotes.
